materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure explicitly links the foundry strategy to internal structural risks and cites specific historical business exits (Optane, NAND, 5G modem) as context for the difficulty of strategic pivots. The 2025 filing lacks this specific contextual linkage and history, focusing instead on different risks like cybersecurity or supply chain. This removal obscures the historical precedent and scale of Intel's strategic restructuring efforts, which is material to understanding the execution risk of the foundry model.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks in New Product Development and AI Execution
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD faces intense competition and rapid technological change in the AI market, with significant risks related to developing, qualifying, and shipping new products on time. Delays can cause missed customer design windows, while uncertainty in long-term AI adoption and potential failure to achieve return on investment pose material risks. The company cannot guarantee success against competitors like Nvidia or customers developing internal solutions, and product complexity necessitates successful high-value launches to maintain average selling prices and competitive positioning.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose that implementing new business strategies and investing in new products/technologies involves inherent risks and does not guarantee success. Intel specifically cites internal structural changes required for its foundry strategy, including a new ERP system, as part of this risk. AMD highlights that its success depends on the timely development and qualification of new products to meet evolving industry trends, noting that failure to do so could cause it to lose competitive positioning. Both emphasize that strategic pivots and new product introductions are complex and risky endeavors.

sentences.text: Our implementation of new business strategies and investments in new businesses, products, and technologies are inherently risky and do not always succeed.

The implementation of our internal foundry operating model requires many internal structural, system, and process changes to support the separation of the product and manufacturing sides of our business and our external foundry business, including a new enterprise resource planning system.

Our ability to identify industry changes, and adapt our strategy to develop, qualify and distribute, and have manufactured, new products and related technologies to meet evolving industry trends and requirements, at prices acceptable to our customers and on a timely basis, are significant factors in determining our competitiveness in our target markets.
Moreover, our investments in new products and technologies involve certain risks and uncertainties and could disrupt our ongoing business.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is implementing a new enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, which may introduce quality issues or programming errors, disrupt operations, and impose demands on management, potentially harming operating results or financial reporting capabilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA explicitly identify the implementation of a new enterprise resource planning (ERP) system as a specific risk associated with their internal structural and process changes. Intel states that its foundry operating model requires a new ERP system to support the separation of product and manufacturing sides. NVIDIA discloses that it continues to design and implement updated accounting functionality related to a new ERP system, warning that such implementations may introduce quality issues or programming errors that could disrupt business operations or financial reporting.

We continue to design and implement updated accounting functionality related to a new enterprise resource planning, or ERP, system.

Any ERP system implementation may introduce problems, such as quality issues or programming errors, that could have an impact on our continued ability to successfully operate our business or to timely and accurately report our financial results.
